_comment: Sovereign source of truth. No digest may be hardcoded anywhere else.
Digests marked sha256:0000... require an authenticated dhi.io login to resolve;
see SETUP-ENVIRONMENTS.md step 7. Every other digest was resolved live on
2026-08-18 and should be re-checked with `make -f Ops.mk verify-pins`.
CODEOWNERS puts this file under @infrashift/security-admins: a `track` widening
is a one-character edit that silently converts every future release from a
reviewed decision into an automated bump.

ory.note: All four Ory services release in lockstep off a shared tag. A partial bump is a bug; drift-upstream.yml must propose all four together.

nats.shortCommitNote: goreleaser stamps {{.ShortCommit}}, whose length is git's DYNAMIC abbreviation for the full repo. Verified empirically: the released v2.14.5 binary embeds 9 characters. It cannot be derived from our build, because fetch-source.sh makes a --depth 1 clone and git then abbreviates to the 7-char minimum. Pinning it as data is the only way to reproduce the vendor's binary; drift PRs must update it alongside `commit`.
nats.note: Moved up from the 2.11 line the user ran previously. Upstream pins GOTOOLCHAIN and uses -trimpath, so this is the one service where a byte-identical cross-check is realistic.

dapr.note: One source repo produces all three images. Moved up from 1.14.4, which is outside Dapr's N-2 support window. Scheduler is included because from 1.15+ actor reminders and workflows require it. Pinned to an untagged commit on release-1.18, deliberately: v1.18.3 vendors etcd 3.5.30, which carries GO-2026-6107 and GO-2026-6114, both High with an upstream fix and therefore blocking under our policy. No released version clears them -- v1.18.3 is the newest tag -- but the fix is backported and this commit is it. ref must be OCI-tag-safe: build-leg.sh interpolates it into DEST_TAG=pr-<n>-<ref>-<arch>, and a '+' there is rejected by the registry grammar, which surfaces only as buildah exit 125. Hence v1.18.4-pre.233f2b49 rather than a semver build-metadata suffix -- it is also the honest ordering, since this commit is on release-1.18 and precedes the v1.18.4 tag. `track` is unchanged, so drift-upstream will propose v1.18.4 as soon as it is tagged; replace this pin with that tag when it lands.

web-ui.note: The compiled web UI. A source build without Node and pnpm has no UI (`builtinassets` embeds web/ui/static, which only `make assets` populates), and upstream publishes this tarball for exactly that case -- its Makefile honours PREBUILT_ASSETS_STATIC_DIR. Its paths are static/..., the shape scripts/package_assets.sh writes. sha256 copied 2026-10-01 from the release's sha256sums.txt. Prometheus does not sign release assets, so this hash IS the trust claim. A drift bump moves the URL but cannot re-pin the hash; scripts/fetch-assets.sh refuses a URL that does not name the release being built.

prometheus.note: Initial pin, the newest release (2026-09-24). Track is the 3.15 minor line, like nats. Upstream's .promu.yml builds with Go 1.27; go.mod only requires 1.26.0, so our go1.26 toolchain builds it with GOTOOLCHAIN=local (no toolchain download) and the cross-check is best-effort.

go1.26.note: Also the donor for /usr/share/zoneinfo, which ubi9-micro does not ship.

ubi9-micro.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-18: ships NO CA trust bundle, NO tzdata, and NO UID 1001 in /etc/passwd. It DOES have bash, coreutils and glibc, so RUN works. Registry path is trusted-base-images, not trusted-base-oci-images (the sibling's directory name differs from its git remote). arm64 is published as arm64/v8; always pin by digest.

ubi9-minimal.note: Donor for /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem only. Assert the copied bundle is >100000 bytes so a truncated one fails loudly.

traefik.reason: Placeholder digests resolved 2026-08-24 with an authenticated dhi.io login (regctl manifest head, index digest). DHI repoints 3-debian13 itself, so the tag string never changes and only the digest moves; track is therefore an exact match.

postgres.reason: Initial pin, runtime + dev. PostgreSQL 17 added 2026-09-15 as a second pair of variants (runtime17/dev17) rather than a second image entry, so both majors are served from one trusted/postgres repository under their own upstream tags. It exists because the platform runs PostgreSQL 17 in two places -- GitLab's database and chit-server -- and this line published only 16, so neither could leave Docker Hub: a PG17 data directory cannot be read by PG16, which makes it a dump-and-restore migration rather than a swap. CONSUMER CAUTION, and it is not the major version: 17-debian is debian-13 while the images it would replace are bookworm (debian-12). A different glibc is a different collation, so text index ordering can change -- REINDEX stored data after the move, exactly as for an alpine-to-debian move. Exact tags rather than a regex range, for the reason the 16 pair has them: only the digest moves, and drift-upstream proposes it.

nexus3.reason: Tracks the 3.90 patch line only; 3.91.0-ubi and 3.91.1-ubi already exist upstream, so a naive newest-tag check would jump a minor on its first run. Trust class none: public Docker Hub image with unsigned BuildKit attestations only. Onboarded in `observe` until the day-one CVE triage lands in exceptions.yaml -- a ~700MB JVM image will very likely quarantine.

notation.trustedIdentity: x509.subject: CN=Microsoft SCD Products RSA Signing,O=Microsoft Corporation,L=Redmond,ST=Washington,C=US
notation.note: Root pinned by TOFU on 2026-09-11 from Microsoft's PKI endpoint; SHA-256 fingerprint 23:FF:E2:B8:BD:B9:A1:71:15:15:D4:CF:FD:A0:4B:C7:F7:93:D5:13:C7:6C:24:3F:10:20:50:7D:86:69:B7:DB, valid to 2047-02-17. The signing leaf (CN=Microsoft SCD Products RSA Signing, expires 2027-10-31) chains via CN=Microsoft SCD Products RSA CA. Identity is pinned to the leaf subject because the root alone would trust every Microsoft product signature. Verified locally with notation v1.3.2 at level strict on 2026-09-11; a wrong root, a wrong identity and an out-of-scope registry each failed as expected.

mssql.reason: Pin moved 2026-09-15 from 2025-CU8-GDR1-rhel-10 (17.0.4085.5, sha256:54b58c3a) to 2025-CU9-rhel-10 (17.0.5005.3), the manifest 2025-latest now resolves to. Same repository, same RHEL 10 base, same bare amd64 manifest shape, Notary signature still present as an OCI referrer. This is the FIRST observed move of this rolling tag and it confirms the shape the initial pin predicted. Initial pin was SQL Server 2025 on the RHEL 10 base (mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/rhel/server, not the Ubuntu mssql/server repo) to match the repo's UBI posture. Rolling tag: Microsoft repoints 2025-latest on every CU and GDR, and a CU regex track would be a trap because `sort -V` orders 2025-CU8-GDR1-rhel-10 BEFORE 2025-CU8-rhel-10, so drift-upstream.sh would never propose a GDR security release. Track is therefore the exact tag and only the digest moves. Note this move goes GDR -> CU, which a CU-ordered track would also have mishandled. Trust class notation: the image carries a Notary Project signature as an OCI referrer, chained to Microsoft Supply Chain RSA Root CA 2022, which we vendor and verify against with the signing identity pinned. There is no cosign signature and no SBOM or provenance referrer, so no attestations are required of this class. Still `observe` until the day-one CVE triage lands in exceptions.yaml; CU9 is newer than the CU8-GDR1 it replaces, so the finding count should not rise.
mssql.note: amd64 ONLY, and a BARE manifest: the tag resolves to a single application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json with no index. Microsoft supports x86-64 hosts only and states emulation is untested. scripts/manifest-platforms.sh derives the platform set from the config os/arch for this shape. Runtime config: user mssql, port 1433, entrypoint /opt/mssql/bin/launch_sqlservr.sh, no declared volumes (data lives under /var/opt/mssql; mount it). The container starts only with ACCEPT_EULA=Y and a password supplied via the MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD environment variable at run time; MSSQL_PID defaults to developer and selecting a production edition asserts that the consumer holds a licence. The SQL build number is not in the tag; read the com.microsoft.version label from the evidence. The notation signature is an OCI referrer in the image's own repository; the mirror copies it with --referrers, and the first run's upstream-referrers.json should list artifactType application/vnd.cncf.notary.signature.

whoami.reason: Traefik's whoami echo server, the test backend infrashift/ansible-collection-infrashift-hashistack's sm-ingress runs behind the edge; it ran docker.io/traefik/whoami:latest. Pinned to v1.12.0, the release :latest resolves to on 2026-09-30 (same index digest). Track is the v1 release line: whoami is a stateless test fixture with no data or config contract, so a minor bump carries nothing a patch-only track would protect, and the regex excludes the per-arch (-amd64/-arm64/-armv7) and two-part rolling (v1.12) tags. Three platforms, not two: the upstream index carries linux/arm/v7, and a mirror copies the whole index, so the declared set must include it or PLATFORM_SET_MISMATCH denies. Trust class none: no cosign signature and no OCI referrers, only unsigned BuildKit attestation manifests inside the index. A scratch image holding one static Go binary with no USER, so it reports root (RUNTIME_RUNS_AS_ROOT, a warning); the binary needs no privilege except a port below 1024, so consumers run it as a non-root uid on an unprivileged port (--user 65532:65532 --port=8080, proven 2026-09-30). Onboarded in `observe` until the day-one CVE triage lands in exceptions.yaml; expect Go standard-library findings from the toolchain it was built with.

crosscheck.note: The -distroless tag, NOT the bare v26.2.0 tag. The bare tag is the Alpine/musl CGO_ENABLED=1 -tags=sqlite,hsm,json1 build (User 10000, 3.6MB base layer) and is not comparable to ours. Ory's cosign signature has Cert:false/Chain:false and no published public key, so we pin by digest and do not claim to verify it.

kratos.reason: Initial pin. No official UBI-based Ory image exists; built from source onto ubi9-micro.

hydra.reason: Initial pin. Note the module path carries /v2. Hydra has no .docker/Dockerfile-build (it has Dockerfile-local-build); the ldflags paths come from .goreleaser.yml.

build.note: Keto's .docker/Dockerfile-build sets CGO_ENABLED=1, but that is the dev build. The released -distroless image is CGO-free and keto's sqlite driver is modernc.org/sqlite (pure Go), so CGO is not needed. Verify `keto migrate up` works before trusting this.
Oathkeeper stamps into package x, NOT driver/configuration. Confirmed from .goreleaser.yml at v26.2.0. Getting this wrong is silent: the binary compiles and reports `dev`.

oathkeeper.reason: Initial pin. Upstream's .docker/Dockerfile-build has a bug (COPY oryx/go.sum proto/go.sum); we do not use it.

nats.archNote: Upstream also publishes arm/v6, arm/v7, 386, ppc64le, s390x and loong64. We build linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only.

build.note: Flags mirror upstream .goreleaser.yml exactly: -trimpath, CGO_ENABLED=0, GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.5, -w (not -s -w). serverVersion takes the tag; gitCommit takes goreleaser's .ShortCommit.

crosscheck.note: Second, independent anchor: the official image does not compile the binary, it downloads the GitHub release tarball and verifies these sha256 values inline in nats-docker/2.14.x/alpine3.22/Dockerfile. Both were confirmed to match on 2026-08-18, and the binary inside the official image is byte-identical to the released tarball. Re-confirmed for v2.14.7 on 2026-09-30: the hashes equal both the release's SHA256SUMS and nats-docker fe222b5f97 (2.14.x/alpine3.22/Dockerfile at NATS_SERVER=2.14.7), and the nats-server in each 2.14.7-alpine3.22 child is byte-identical to its tarball's (amd64 and arm64). TIER DOWNGRADED from flag-matched to best-effort after empirical testing: we reproduced every observable build input -- Go 1.26.5, identical dep set, -trimpath, CGO_ENABLED=0, GOAMD64=v1, DefaultGODEBUG, mod=v2.14.5, vcs.revision/time/modified=false, and the 9-char short commit -- and the binary still differs. Whatever remains is not visible in `go version -m`. Do not treat a NATS mismatch as alarming until someone identifies the residual input.

runtime.configNote: Ours, not upstream's. nats-docker ships a cluster block with hardcoded credentials ruser/T0pS3cr3t. All three ports are >1024 so non-root binding is fine.

nats.reason: Initial pin on the 2.14 line, moved up from the 2.11-alpine image previously in use.

daprd.archNote: Upstream index is a Docker manifest list that also contains windows/amd64 and linux/arm/v7. Cross-check pins per-platform tags so extraction never depends on runtime manifest-list resolution.

runtime.userNote: Upstream runs 65532:65532 and the Dapr Helm chart pins runAsUser: 65532. We use 1001 per repo convention, so a Helm deployment needs an override. The /daprd compat symlink exists because the injector may emit command: ["/daprd"].
runtime.portNote: Ports are from documentation, not from the pinned source. VERIFY against cmd/daprd options before relying on them.

daprd.reason: Initial pin. Moved up from 1.14.4, which is outside Dapr's N-2 support window.

crosscheck.note: daprio/placement is the dedicated single-binary image. daprio/dapr is the kitchen-sink image carrying all six control-plane binaries and is the wrong cross-check source.

runtime.portNote: From documentation. VERIFY against cmd/placement options.

dapr-placement.reason: Initial pin. Built from the same source checkout as daprd and dapr-scheduler; sources.dapr.lockstep prevents drift.

runtime.portNote: From documentation. VERIFY against cmd/scheduler options.
runtime.volumeNote: The scheduler keeps an embedded etcd store; confirm the default data dir at the pinned tag before relying on this path.

dapr-scheduler.reason: Initial pin. Required from Dapr 1.15+ for actor reminders and workflows; the user is migrating from 1.14 where it did not exist.

prometheus.archNote: Upstream's index also carries arm/v7, ppc64le, riscv64 and s390x. We build linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only.

build.note: Binaries, tags and ldflags are upstream's .promu.yml at v3.15.0. Version takes the ref WITHOUT the leading v (promu stamps {{.Version}} from the VERSION file, 3.15.0). BuildDate is the source commit date, not wall-clock, so a rerun stamps the same string. promtool ships on purpose: it is the image's only HTTP client (ubi9-micro has no curl), and consumers use `promtool check healthy --http.config.file` as a health check that can present a client certificate.

crosscheck.note: Upstream's own image (busybox base, USER nobody, ENTRYPOINT /bin/prometheus), per-platform children of the v3.15.0 index sha256:efd719c9... resolved 2026-10-01. Unsigned, so trust class none. best-effort: upstream compiles with Go 1.27 and we use 1.26, so a mismatch is expected and proves nothing.

runtime.configNote: CMD and /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml are upstream's (documentation/examples/prometheus.yml, from the pinned source tree), so the image runs standalone exactly as quay.io/prometheus/prometheus does. Real deployments mount their own config, and a web config for TLS.

prometheus.reason: Initial pin. No usable UBI-based Prometheus exists: Red Hat's registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-prometheus-rhel9 needs an entitled, authenticated pull and ships OpenShift's fork on the OCP release train (v4.22), not upstream; DHI's is Debian-based. Built from source onto ubi9-micro. Onboarded in observe per adding-an-upstream.md; moved to enforce 2026-10-01 after the first review (PR #25) came back clean on both arches: allow=true, blocking=0, waived=0, 6 recorded (non-blocking), so no exception was needed. Consumer: infrashift/ansible-collection-infrashift-hashistack terraform/live/prometheus.
